A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete research work, including Appendices A–E. Pages 2–46 have identical extracted text and rendered images; differences are confined to first-page editorial and presentation details.

before.justification: v3 reports original kernel simulations and experiments on synthetic data, MNIST, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains those original empirical results, including the matched-training-loss comparison in Appendix A.2 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The residual scaling formulation, ResNet/RNTK setup, training procedures and mirrored initialization in Appendix B.1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic sphere data and MNIST, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet tasks. Section 4 and Appendix A contain identical evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The base and normalization comparisons are unchanged. Table 1 retains the same Base, Fixup, ReZero and DeepNorm comparators against Proposed.

E3.justification: Data splits, metrics, model configurations, learning rates and training schedules match. Appendix A.2 retains the same comparison at training loss approximately 0.05.

E4.justification: The scaling-exponent and depth analyses in Section 4, and the matched-training-loss analysis in Appendix A.2, retain identical questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 retains averaging over 100 random input pairs and standard-error shading. No repeated-run information or uncertainty reporting is added, removed or revised.

E6.justification: All plotted results and Table 1 entries are identical. For example, matched MNIST accuracy remains 96.66% for Base and 97.29% for Proposed.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions, theorems and derivations in Sections 1–3, together with all proofs in Appendices B–E, are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same claims about uniform RNTK convergence, poor generalization under constant scaling, and minimax rates with rapidly decaying scaling and early stopping.

C2.justification: Interpretations distinguishing generalization benefits from optimization benefits are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning theoretical assumptions, regression guarantees and small-scale image-classification experiments.

D1.justification: Implementation, initialization and hyperparameter disclosures match throughout the main text and appendices. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, novelty positioning and reference list are identical.

P1.justification: On page 1, Songtao Tian's correspondence marker changes from ‡ to †, and the arXiv stamp changes from v3, 25 May 2026, to v4, 30 Aug 2026. All other wording and document structure match.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. Figures 1–7, Table 1 and all remaining page layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 changes only the correspondence marker and the version/date stamp and its placement. The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, reproducibility information and appendices remain identical, so these administrative edits produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
